title: Wterm speed, truth, and visual stability
description:
# Wterm speed, truth, and visual stability

## Background
The public BB plugin `wterm-terminal-preview` (repo `bb-wterm-terminal-plugin`, v0.3.16) already attaches a Ghostty-backed terminal to a BB thread with uploads, Nerd Font, OSC 52, and a legacy WebSocket path. Users still feel a slow, empty, jumpy first experience in the BB web app: blank/white first paint, “session unavailable” right after create, multi-tab verify stalls, zombie `running` reconnects, TUI color stripes in scrollback, wheel/resize jump-to-bottom, extra token fetches, uncached 1.2MB font reads, and `@wterm` 0.3.4 installed against a 0.4.0 lockfile.

## Goal (principal)
Make the installed Wterm preview in BB web open quickly, stay visually stable, and remain correct under multi-tab create/verify. Canonical claims: ISA.md ISC-11+. ISC-1–ISC-10 (standalone security/ordering suite) stay closed and must remain green.

## Architecture spine (do not invert)
1. `npm ci` to 0.4.0 before renderer archaeology.
2. `withLinkedTerminalIds` is write-only; listSessions must not hold it across `terminals.get`.
3. KV linked IDs expand–contract: read `string[]` or `{id, firstUnavailableAt}[]`.
4. Synthetic missing sessions are `unavailable`, never `running`.
5. One plugin-token cache shared by renderer and upload panel.
6. Do not lift WebSocket attachment across panel unmount until headed BB proves it (ISA fog).
7. Do not implement `experimental_primarySurface`, font subsetting, vendor compileStreaming, or delete `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

## Children
All phase beads in this workspace. Close this epic only when F1–F5 ISC are verified and F6 is either verified headed or explicitly deferred in ISA Decisions with reason (no headed BB).

## Test plan
- Every child: `npm test` (ISC-32)
- After server/package: omit-dev build (ISC-33) when feasible
- No imports outside this repo (ISC-35)
- Headed BB: ISC-36–38

## Considerations
Plugin ID stays `wterm-terminal-preview`. Pinned: zod 4.3.6, vitest 4.1.10, plugin-sdk 0.4.21. Reserve `server.ts`, `app.tsx`, `wterm-renderer.tsx` if agents run in parallel.
close_reason: F1–F5 children closed with ISC evidence. F6 headed on BB 38896 thr_fgn2njixb7: term_7d8wrt626z vs term_3gwkt6m52p, fresh 0.3.16 prompt, remount unavail=[], npm test 13/97. Fog .16 closed without attachment lift. Independent review: run() always createTerminal; no last-id hydrate; picker New terminal creates; loadLinkedTerminals gets outside write mutex; synthetic unavailable; follow-bottom on instance.element; dark loading CSS. ISC-30 dropped. PERF-03 stays fog.

comments.text: Polish 2: F7 new-tab-is-new-session. Dropped Reopen last. Ready work is still .1 npm ci.

comments.text: Accounting 2026-09-04: ISA phase complete, 46/46. ISC-30 DROPPED marked resolved. ISC-43: live composer uses wtermOpenCount (reveal vs create), not resolveSessionTerminalId. Fog .16 closed without attachment lift. Release 0.3.17.

title: Align installed @wterm to lockfile 0.4.0
description:
# Align installed @wterm to lockfile 0.4.0

## Background
ISA ISC-11, ISC-12, ISC-13. ANALYSIS BUG-01. `package.json` declares `@wterm/* ^0.4.0` and `package-lock.json` contains 0.4.0, but `node_modules` has been observed at 0.3.4. Repo-root `ghostty-vt.wasm` (577013 bytes) matches 0.4.0; `dist/ghostty-vt.wasm` (434450 bytes) matched the stale 0.3.4 tree. Tests and local renderer then run a different emulator than production `dist/`. Private `terminal._measureCharSize` used in `wterm-renderer.tsx` may differ across versions.

## Why this is first
Any CSS/measure/scroll patch against the wrong ABI is wasted. Phase 0 is a gate for all other beads.

## Technical approach
From repo root only:
```
npm ci
npm ls @wterm/dom @wterm/ghostty @wterm/react
npm run build
npm test
sha256sum ghostty-vt.wasm dist/ghostty-vt.wasm
```
Do not hand-copy wasm. Do not bump to 0.4.1 unless hashes/docs require it (ANALYSIS: 0.4.0 vs 0.4.1 wasm sha equal). Do not delete `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

If `_measureCharSize` is missing after ci: do not invent a fork. Note in ISA `## Not yet specified` / Decisions and leave font-size refit to public API. Do not block this bead on that fog if versions and hashes and tests are green.

## Success criteria
- node_modules `@wterm/dom`, `@wterm/ghostty`, `@wterm/react` all 0.4.0 matching lockfile
- sha256 of `dist/ghostty-vt.wasm` equals sha256 of `ghostty-vt.wasm`
- `npm test` exits 0

## Test plan
- `npm ls` output captured
- `npm test` full suite (existing ISC-1–10 coverage)
- hash equality command

## Considerations
`npm ci` mutates node_modules and dist. Runtime `npm install --omit=dev` path must still work later (ISC-33) but is not this bead’s only gate. No feature code in this bead.
close_reason: npm ci: @wterm/dom,ghostty,react all 0.4.0. npm run build copies ghostty-vt.wasm (bb plugin build does not). sha256 4a0a02357206349ed52b76ebda8feea4a65e453fe4e199832d8c009d7c41ba4f equal root/dist/node_modules. npm test 10 files / 68 tests pass. _measureCharSize still private on 0.4.0; no fork. Stay on 0.4.0 not 0.4.1.

title: Synthetic missing sessions are unavailable, not running
description:
# Synthetic missing sessions are unavailable, not running

## Background
ISA ISC-26, ISC-27. ANALYSIS §9.2 step 3.

`unavailableLinkedSession` currently sets `status: "running"` and `updatedAt: 0`. Picker shows Running · 01.01.1970. `evaluateTerminalPresence` treats running as `ready`, so the panel opens a WebSocket to a missing PTY and `scheduleReconnect` loops forever with no error.

Intent of `running` was “don’t kill the tab on a blip.” TTL bead covers blips. Lying about health is worse.

## Technical approach
Plugin `Session` status for synthetic rows: `"unavailable"`.
`isActiveStatus` in `terminal-open-policy.ts` already allows only `running` and `starting` → presence `missing` automatically. Confirm tests.

Picker: unavailable sessions go to Exited (or a dedicated section). Restart button should still work using existing restart RPC. Do not list them as Running.

Upload `sessionsForThread` must not treat unavailable as an active terminal for path/auth.

Do not change real SDK session statuses returned by successful `terminals.get`.

## Success criteria
- Fixture unavailable synthetic status is `unavailable`
- Policy: that session is not `ready`
- No infinite reconnect from treating zombie as ready (unit: presence missing)
- Picker classification: not in Running

## Test plan
- `server.test.ts` listed sessions
- `terminal-open-policy.test.ts` inactive/unavailable
- picker partition test if helper extracted
- `npm test`

## Considerations
Depends on TTL+read-path for a complete zombie story but can land the status string first with tests. Coordinate `Session` type in one place.
close_reason: ISC-26/27: unavailableLinkedSession status unavailable; evaluateTerminalPresence missing on attempt 1; partitionRunningExited puts zombies in Exited; upload 404s unavailable ids. npm test 13 files / 97 pass.

title: Single retryable plugin-token cache
description:
# Single retryable plugin-token cache

## Background
ISA ISC-22. ANALYSIS PERF-01.

`wterm-renderer.tsx` caches POST `/api/v1/plugins/wterm-terminal-preview/token` via `createRetryablePromiseCache`. `terminal-panel.tsx` has a **separate** `pluginToken(signal)` for uploads. First open + upload = up to 3 token POSTs. Both already use zod parse `{token: string}` and 10s timeout.

## Technical approach
New `plugin-token.ts`:
- PLUGIN_ID `wterm-terminal-preview`
- export `getPluginToken` from `createRetryablePromiseCache` in `retryable-cache.ts`
- fetch POST, parse, throw on failure (keep current error text)

Replace both call sites. AbortSignal: do **not** abort the shared in-flight token because an upload unmounted. Use AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) inside the cache factory. Callers may ignore extra signal or race their own timeout without calling abort on the shared fetch.

## Success criteria
- Two concurrent callers → one fetch
- Renderer WASM/font and panel upload both import the module
- Failure still retries per existing retryable-cache semantics

## Test plan
- `plugin-token.test.ts` with mocked `global.fetch`
- `retryable-cache.test.ts` still green
- `npm test`

## Considerations
Do not put token in localStorage. Do not change auth to query-string (ISA fog / security). Easy parallel to server beads (different files).
close_reason: ISC-22: plugin-token.ts getPluginToken shared by renderer and panel. Concurrent fetch once. npm test 83 pass.

title: Ordered replay insert without full sort on every chunk
description:
# Ordered replay insert without full sort on every chunk

## Background
ISA ISC-31, must preserve ISC-8. ANALYSIS PERF-04.

`flushWhenReplayComplete` copies `pendingReplay` Map values and `.sort((l,r)=>l.seq-r.seq)` on every chunk. Long replay (~1000 lines) repeats O(n log n). Map insertion order is not seq order.

ISC-8: replay output is delivered before buffered live output without duplicate sequences. Queued input/resize (ISC-9) must still flush once after open.

## Technical approach
Keep uniqueness by seq. On each replay chunk, insert into a list already ordered by seq (binary search or linear findIndex for small n — n is replay size; linear is fine and simpler than a tree). Flush walks the array. Live buffer still waits until replay complete.

Do not drop duplicate-seq protection. Do not flush live first.

Extend existing `terminal-attachment.test.ts` ordering fixtures; add out-of-order replay chunks (seq 3 then 1 then 2) asserting emit order 1,2,3 then live.

## Success criteria
- Out-of-order replay still emits increasing seq
- No duplicate seq emitted
- Live still after replay
- `npm test` including old fixtures

## Test plan
- Existing attachment tests + new out-of-order insert
- Logging: assertion messages with seq lists

## Considerations
Same file as encodeBase64. Prefer one agent doing both or encode first then this. Do not micro-optimize with a heap.
close_reason: ISC-31: ordered pendingReplay insert; out-of-order 1 then 0 then 2 emits 0,1,2 then live. ISC-8 fixtures green. npm test 83 pass.

title: Follow-bottom must track the inner scrolling .wterm element
description:
# Follow-bottom must track the inner scrolling .wterm element

## Background
ISA ISC-17. ANALYSIS FLICKER-03.

`WtermRenderer` attaches `onScroll` to the outer `div.wterm-renderer` which is `overflow: hidden`. Actual scroll is on inner `.wterm` / `instance.element`. `followBottomRef` stays true, so every resize/output forces `scrollTop = scrollHeight` — user reading history is yanked down. Combined with `contain: layout paint` inside @wterm and font-size refit rAF, this is the jump-flicker.

## Technical approach
In `handleReady`, if `instance.element` exists, add passive `scroll` listener:
`followBottomRef.current = el.scrollHeight - el.scrollTop - el.clientHeight <= 1`
Remove outer `onScroll` if it never fires usefully.
Cleanup listener on unmount / replace instance.

Do not “fix” font-size by extra `getBoundingClientRect` loops (FLICKER-02 / O-10 is research; out of scope unless trivial). After @wterm 0.4.0 align, confirm `instance.element` is the scroller; if class is different, still bind the element that has scrollHeight.

When followBottom is false, output and font-size effects must not assign scrollTop to bottom.

## Success criteria
- Stub element not at bottom → followBottom false
- Further output does not force bottom in that state
- At bottom (delta <= 1px) still follows

## Test plan
- Extend `wterm-renderer.test.ts` with a fake instance.element
- If renderer tests cannot mount Terminal, extract `computeFollowBottom(el)` + `shouldStickToBottom`
- `npm test`

## Considerations
File overlap with loading skeleton and wheel guard. Keep diffs to handleReady + listener + remove outer onScroll. Headed confirmation is F6.
close_reason: ISC-17: computeFollowBottom on instance.element; outer onScroll removed; font-size effect assigns scrollTop only when shouldRestoreBottom. npm test 13 files / 97 pass.

# Headed BB web smoke: paint, create, two distinct tabs

## Background

BB with plugin sourced. agent-browser or human session.

title: [FOG] Lift LegacyTerminalAttachment across panel hide
description:
# [FOG] Lift LegacyTerminalAttachment across panel hide — do not implement yet

## Background
ISA Not yet specified: panel unmount vs module-level attachment map. ANALYSIS PERF-03.

`useLegacyTerminalAttachment` constructs `LegacyTerminalAttachment`, `connect()`, and `detach()` on unmount. BB tab hide remounts `TerminalPanel` → WS tear-down. WASM/font caches survive; the socket does not. History claimed a partial “keep sessions alive across panel closes” for assets only.

## Why this is a bead
So it is not forgotten and so agents do **not** silently implement it in another slice.

## Technical approach when unblocked
Only after headed BB proves: (a) hide/show remounts the panel, (b) reconnect cost is user-visible, (c) lifting to SelectedTerminal or `Map<terminalId, attachment>` does not leak after real tab close / thread switch.

Until then: status stays deferred / blocked on headed smoke findings.

## Success criteria for later implementation (not now)
- Hide/show does not reconnect WS
- Close tab / thread still detaches and does not leak
- ISC-9.2 still true: detach does not send PTY close

## Test plan
- Attachment lifecycle tests + headed

## Considerations
Priority P3. Do not start. Do not fork @wterm for compileStreaming in this bead either.

title: New Wterm tab always opens a new session, never last PTY
description:
# New Wterm tab always opens a new session, never last PTY

## Background
ISA F7 ISC-39, ISC-40, ISC-41, ISC-42, ISC-43. Principal 2026-09-04: a new terminal / new tab must open a new session, not the previous one.

README already claims every Wterm tab starts an independent session. `threadPanelAction.run` does `createTerminal` then `openPanel({ params: { terminalId } })`. Other paths steal last PTY:

1. **`LegacyTerminalAction`**: `currentParams = hasTerminalParams(params) ? params : fallbackParams` from **thread-scoped** localStorage. A new tab with empty host params **is** the previous terminal.
2. **Composer `OpenSessionTerminalAction`**: passes `readLastTerminalId` into `revealSessionTerminalPanel`. Fine only if it reveals an already-open panel. A newly created panel must not steal last id.
3. **`resolveSessionTerminalId`** hardcodes `openTabCount: 0`, so `reusableTerminalId` always considers reuse even when tabs are mounted/pending. `wtermOpenCount` already exists (mounted + pending).
4. Planned picker “Reopen last” (ISC-30) is dropped.

Same-tab remount without host params: empty params must show Picker, not last id. Losing remount convenience is better than every new tab being last PTY. Do not invent a second thread-scoped fallback.

## Technical approach
- Keep `run()` always `createTerminal` + params = new id.
- Extract `initialPanelParams(hostParams): host | null` — never reads localStorage. `LegacyTerminalAction` uses that. Still **write** last id when a real session is shown.
- `resolveSessionTerminalId` takes `openTabCount` (default from `wtermOpenCount(threadId)` at call site). Composer reveal: if a Wterm tab is already open, reveal it; if this gesture opens a new panel/tab, `createTerminal`.
- Tests: last id in storage + empty host params → not that id; `openTabCount > 0` → no reuse; existing `reusableTerminalId` tests stay.
- Coordinate `app.tsx` with picker bead (`wterm-speed-feel-ftz.6`): this bead owns last-id/open policy; picker owns loading/failed UI. Prefer implementing this after picker in the same file (depends on .6) to reduce merge fights, or one agent both.

## Success criteria
- New tab + stored last id + empty params does not mount last session
- `run()` always creates
- Picker New terminal creates
- Composer does not bind a new tab to last id when openTabCount > 0
- Two sequential new tabs → two distinct ids (headed ISC-42)

## Test plan
- `initialPanelParams` unit
- `session-terminal-composer.test.ts` openTabCount cases (update the three tests that assume reuse with implicit 0)
- `terminal-open-policy.test.ts` already has openTabCount > 0 → null; keep
- `npm test`

## Considerations
HostTerminalAction already uses host params only — do not add localStorage there. Do not delete `readLastTerminalId`; still written after create/select. P0.
close_reason: ISC-39/40/41/43: run() always createTerminal; initialPanelParams ignores last-id; picker New terminal creates; resolveSessionTerminalId takes openTabCount; composer reveals without last id when a tab is open. npm test 13 files / 97 pass.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Polish 1: composer hardcodes openTabCount 0 — pass wtermOpenCount. Empty host params = Picker, not last id (ISC-43).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Polish 2: serialize after picker (.6) because both edit app.tsx. HostTerminalAction already param-only; do not add storage there. Remount-without-params shows Picker; that is preferred to stealing last PTY.

title: Dark loading skeleton and transparent TUI scrollback rows
description:
# Dark loading skeleton and transparent TUI scrollback rows

## Background
ISA ISC-14, ISC-15. ANALYSIS FLICKER-01 and BUG-02.

`WtermRenderer` currently returns an unstyled empty `div.wterm-renderer` while Ghostty WASM/core is null → white/blank flash (200–600ms) then another hop when replay arrives. `@wterm/dom` promotes last-cell background onto `div.term-row`; we already force `.term-row { background: transparent !important }` for normal-shell after TUI, but `.term-scrollback-row` is not covered, so Herdr/vim colors remain as stripes in history.

## Technical approach
`wterm-renderer.css`:
- Selector list: `.wterm-renderer .term-row, .wterm-renderer .term-scrollback-row` with transparent background and no box-shadow.
- `.wterm-renderer--loading` uses `var(--term-bg, #1e1e1e)`.
- `::after` muted cursor bar with blink; `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` disable animation.

`wterm-renderer.tsx` when `!core`: add class `--loading`, `aria-busy="true"`, `aria-label="Terminal loading"`.

Do not wait for attachment ready to show this skeleton. Do not change WASM load itself here.

## Success criteria
- Scrollback rows cannot keep TUI row background via our CSS override
- First paint without core is dark, not unstyled empty
- Reduced motion honored

## Test plan
- Unit/source test: CSS file contains both selectors
- Renderer test: loading branch className includes `wterm-renderer--loading`
- `npm test`
- Optional headed screenshot later (ISC-36 depends on this)

## Considerations
Antecedent for experiential first paint (ISA ISC-15). Coordinate with follow-bottom bead if both edit `wterm-renderer.tsx` — this bead only touches the `!core` return and CSS.
close_reason: ISC-14/15: term-row+term-scrollback-row transparent; --loading dark #1e1e1e + muted cursor; prefers-reduced-motion. Tests: first paint and TUI scrollback. npm test 10 files / 70 tests pass.

title: Skip selection clear on collapsed wheel events
description:
# Skip selection clear on collapsed wheel events

## Background
ISA ISC-16. ANALYSIS FLICKER-04.

`handleWheelCapture` in `wterm-renderer.tsx` calls `clearTerminalSelection(..., window.getSelection())` on every wheel. `getSelection()` + `removeAllRanges()` forces repaint at wheel rate (~60Hz) even when nothing is selected. `clearTerminalSelection` already checks rangeCount internally but the expensive path still runs.

## Technical approach
At the start of `handleWheelCapture`, after the existing `clearSelectionBoundaryRef` guard:
```
const selection = window.getSelection();
if (!selection || selection.isCollapsed) return;
```
Then pass that `selection` into `clearTerminalSelection` instead of calling `getSelection` twice.

Keep existing behavior when a real range exists (TUI mouse / native selection inside terminal).

## Success criteria
- Collapsed selection: `removeAllRanges` is not invoked
- Non-collapsed: existing clear still runs

## Test plan
- Prefer testing via `terminal-selection.ts` helper if the guard is lifted there; otherwise unit-test a small exported predicate `shouldClearSelectionOnWheel(selection)` to avoid mounting WASM.
- `npm test`

## Considerations
Do not debounce so hard that a real selection survives wheel when we intend to clear it. Collapsed check is enough. File overlap with loading CSS bead: only the wheel callback.
close_reason: ISC-16: shouldClearSelectionOnWheel skips collapsed/null; handleWheelCapture uses one getSelection. npm test 83 pass.

title: Grace period for evaluateTerminalPresence after create
description:
# Grace period for evaluateTerminalPresence after create

## Background
ISA ISC-19, ISC-20, ISC-21. ANALYSIS BUG-03.

`SelectedTerminal` verifies via `listSessions` immediately after create. `rememberLinkedTerminal` is queued. If verify runs before KV write, `evaluateTerminalPresence` returns `missing` after 3×400ms → “session is no longer available”.

Grace is the client symptom fix; mutex split is the cause. Still need grace because a read snapshot can precede remember.

Does **not** depend on unavailable-status. `isActiveStatus` already only running/starting. Unavailable tests live on that other bead.

## Technical approach
`terminal-open-policy.ts`:
- `maxAttempts` default 6 (was 3)
- `gracePeriodAttempts` default 2
- `sessions === null` → retry if attempt < maxAttempts else existing ready fallback (keep contract)
- found + active → `ready`
- found + inactive → `missing` immediately (no grace)
- not found + attempt <= grace → `retry`
- not found + attempt < maxAttempts → `retry`
- else `missing`

Update `terminal-open-policy.test.ts`. Optional first delay 600ms in `app.tsx`; policy function is the contract.

## Success criteria
- Absent new id during grace → never `missing`
- Inactive present → `missing` on attempt 1
- Exhausted attempts → `missing`

## Test plan
- Exhaustive Vitest on `evaluateTerminalPresence`
- `npm test`

## Considerations
Independent of picker and of unavailable status string. Can land as soon as @wterm is aligned.
close_reason: ISC-19/20/21: maxAttempts 6, gracePeriodAttempts 2. Absent id retries through grace; inactive present missing on attempt 1; exhausted missing. terminal-open-policy.test.ts. npm test 12 files / 83 tests.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Polish: grace is independent of unavailable-status. Removed false dep on .10.

title: Picker loading/failed/loaded (no auto-reopen)
description:
# Picker loading / failed / loaded (no auto-reopen)

## Background
ISA ISC-28, ISC-29. ISC-30 DROPPED (new tab must not reopen last). ANALYSIS §9.3.

`Picker` in `app.tsx` uses `useState<Session[]>([])`. Until `listSessions` returns, UI shows empty Running/Exited. RPC failure also `setItems([])` — looks like success-empty, so users spawn duplicates.

Principal 2026-09-04: a new terminal tab must be a new PTY. Do **not** add “Reopen last terminal” as a default control on this screen. Existing sessions are listed as rows; clicking a row attaches. **New terminal** always `createTerminal`.

## Technical approach
Discriminated union:
`{kind:"loading"} | {kind:"loaded", items:Session[]} | {kind:"failed", message:string}`

Keep generation/mounted guards. `reload` counter for Retry.

UI:
- loading: skeleton in `app.css` + `prefers-reduced-motion`
- failed: role=alert + Retry
- loaded: Running; Exited only if nonempty; empty running copy “No running terminals.”
- New terminal button: existing `creating` path, always create RPC then `replace(newId)`
- Clicking a listed session: `replace({schemaVersion:1, terminalId})` — explicit attach only

Extract `partitionRunningExited` / picker state helpers if needed for tests.

## Success criteria
- Loading ≠ empty loaded ≠ failed
- Failed is not an empty list
- No control that auto-selects `readLastTerminalId` on mount
- New terminal always creates

## Test plan
- `picker-state.test.ts`
- `npm test`

## Considerations

title: In-memory Nerd Font bytes cache on plugin HTTP
description:
# In-memory Nerd Font bytes cache on plugin HTTP

## Background
ISA ISC-23. ANALYSIS §9.1.

`ghosttyWasmBytes` already caches `Uint8Array` + in-flight Promise. Nerd Font GET handler `readFile(bundledNerdFontUrl())` every request (1.2MB). `cache-control: immutable` does not apply to authenticated `fetch` with `x-bb-plugin-token` from `wterm-renderer.tsx` FontFace path. Multi-tab / reload = repeated disk I/O and heap copies in the Node plugin process.

## Technical approach
Copy the WASM pattern in `server.ts`:
- `let nerdFontCache: Promise<Uint8Array> | Uint8Array | null = null`
- `nerdFontBytes()` coalesces in-flight reads, stores a `Uint8Array` copy
- GET route returns `new Response(await nerdFontBytes(), { headers: same as today })`

Do not subset the font. Do not drop `auth: "token"`. Do not change content-type.

Add a test seam: extract `createBytesCache(read)` or spy `readFile` if tests already mock fs. Two overlapping calls must invoke read once.

## Success criteria
- Second GET does not call `readFile` again after first resolves
- Overlapping GETs share one in-flight read
- Headers unchanged

## Test plan
- Extend `server.test.ts` (or a small cache unit test)
- Existing asset tests still pass
- `npm test`

## Considerations
Same file as linked-ID mutex work. Implement cache as a small isolated function at top of `server.ts` so the mutex bead can merge cleanly. Do not hold the linked-ID mutex while reading the font.
close_reason: ISC-23: createBytesCache coalesces overlapping nerd-font reads; GET uses nerdFontBytes. server.test.ts createBytesCache. npm test 83 pass.

title: Read path for linked terminals must not take the write mutex
description:
# Read path for linked terminals must not take the write mutex

## Background
ISA ISC-24. ANALYSIS §9.2 (critical multi-tab stall).

`withLinkedTerminalIds` serializes per-thread KV updates. `loadLinkedTerminals` incorrectly runs **inside** that mutex and awaits `Promise.allSettled(linkedIds.map(terminals.get))` — N host round-trips while holding the exclusive lock. Callers: `listSessions` (verify loop every 400ms, picker), `sessionsForThread` (upload), create/remember, restart. Two tabs → O(tabs × N × RTT) stalls. This also explains BUG-03: verify’s listSessions queues behind the same create’s remember.

## Technical approach
1. `linkedTerminalIds(bb, threadId)` snapshot **without** write lock.
2. Fan-out `terminals.get` **outside** the lock.
3. Return sessions + unavailable ids immediately for RPC.
4. If host returns a replacement id, `void withLinkedTerminalIds` later: re-read `current`, remap only ids still present, `saveLinkedTerminalIds`. Catch and ignore (best-effort).
5. `withLinkedTerminalIds` remains for `rememberLinkedTerminal` and restart rewrites only.

Upload path must use sessions that actually exist; do not authorize upload to unavailable ids.

Concurrency test: delay `terminals.get`; start listSessions; then createTerminal/remember; remember must complete without waiting for the delayed gets.

## Success criteria
- listSessions does not await other listSessions’ host GETs via the write gate
- create remember is not blocked by in-flight list fan-out
- replacement id reconcile does not drop a concurrently remembered new id

## Test plan
- `server.test.ts` fake sdk with controllable delay
- Existing thread-scope upload/restart tests still pass
- `npm test`

## Considerations
Implement after or with KV record parser if signatures change. Do not “fix” by increasing verify retries only. Hot file `server.ts` — one agent with nerd-font-cache and unavailable/TTL if possible.
close_reason: ISC-24: loadLinkedTerminals snapshots KV then fans out terminals.get outside withLinkedTerminalIds. server.test.ts delayed get: createTerminal remember finishes first; reconcile keeps term-new. npm test 13 files / 97 pass.

title: Linked-ID KV expand-contract with dead-ID TTL
description:
# Linked-ID KV expand–contract with dead-ID TTL

## Background
ISA ISC-25. ANALYSIS §9.2 step 2.

`nextLinkedTerminalIds` keeps an id forever when `terminals.get` rejects. N grows for the life of the thread; every listSessions pays N timeouts inside (today) the mutex. Need a bounded list without treating a 1s host blip as death.

## Technical approach
Type:
```
interface LinkedTerminalRecord {
  id: string;
  firstUnavailableAt: number | null;
}
const DEAD_TERMINAL_GRACE_MS = 60_000;
```

`parseLinkedRecords(unknown)`:
- array of strings → `{id, firstUnavailableAt: null}` (legacy)
- array of objects with string `id` → use numeric `firstUnavailableAt` or null
- anything else skipped

On get fulfilled: stamp null (live).
On get rejected: set stamp to now if null; if `now - stamp > 60s`, drop id.
Writes may persist records. Reads must still accept legacy `string[]` forever.

Time: inject a `now: () => number` in the pure function for tests.

Do not require a one-shot migration job.

## Success criteria
- Legacy KV arrays still load
- Live success clears stamp
- Rejected id survives <60s
- Rejected id drops after 60s
- N cannot grow unbounded from permanent failures

## Test plan
- Pure parser + next-state tests (preferred new `linked-terminal-records.ts` so server stays thin)
- `server.test.ts` round-trip if KV mock exists
- `npm test`

## Considerations
Split into `linked-terminal-records.ts` to avoid merge hell with read-path and font cache. Server imports the parser. Clock freeze in tests.
close_reason: ISC-25: linked-terminal-records parse legacy string[], stamp on reject, drop after 60s. server persists records. npm test 83 pass.
